prompt: hpx::future destructor blocking behavior vs std::future
answer:
`hpx::future`’s destructor **never blocks**, even if the asynchronous operation has not completed.

By contrast, a `std::future` returned by `std::async()` **is required to block in its destructor** if its value is not ready. This behavior applies when the future holds the last reference to an unfinished shared state. ([HPX documentation](https://docs.hpx.dev/branches/master/html/manual/writing_distributed_hpx_applications.html), [P0701R2](https://www.open-std.org/JTC1/SC22/WG21/docs/papers/2018/p0701r2.html))

Calling `get()` may still block for either future type until the asynchronous operation completes.
